title: TRACE: A Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Physical Reasoning for Seismology
abstract: arXiv:2603.21152v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Modern seismic networks resolve earthquake sequences in unprecedented detail, yet explaining how large earthquakes emerge from evolving fault systems remains difficult. We introduce TRACE, a seismology-guided artificial intelligence agent that plans and executes workflows while preserving auditable evidence chains from observations to physical interpretation. We evaluated TRACE through 104 benchmark tasks and two complementary earthquake sequences. For the well-studied 2019 Ridgecrest sequence, TRACE constructed a high-resolution catalog from continuous waveforms and retrospectively recovered delayed cascading activation between the Mw 6.4 and Mw 7.1 earthquakes without a prescribed target interpretation. In the less-understood 2025-2026 Sanriku sequence off northeastern Japan, TRACE developed a testable interpretation of progressive destabilization within a segmented megathrust. translated_title: TRACE：一个用于地震学自主物理推理的多智能体系统
translated_abstract: 现代地震台网以前所未有的细节解析地震序列，然而解释大地震如何从不断演化的断裂系统中孕育而生仍然十分困难。我们提出了TRACE，一个以地震学为导向的人工智能智能体，它能够规划和执行工作流程，同时保留从观测到物理解释的可审计证据链。我们通过104个基准测试任务和两个互补的地震序列对TRACE进行了评估。对于研究较为深入的2019年里奇克莱斯特地震序列，TRACE从连续波形数据中构建了高分辨率地震目录，并在没有预设目标解释的情况下，回顾性地恢复了Mw 6.4与Mw 7.1地震之间的延迟级联触发过程。对于认知较少的2025-2026年日本东北近海三陆地震序列，TRACE提出了一个可检验的解释，即分段式巨型逆冲断层内的渐进失稳过程。其综合分析将耦合的地震-非地震活动（此处摘要被截断）
tldr: TRACE是一个地震学导向的多智能体AI系统，能在保留可审计证据链的前提下自主规划和执行地震分析工作流程，成功重现了2019年里奇克莱斯特地震序列的延迟级联激活，并为2025-2026年三陆地震序列的巨型逆冲断层渐进失稳提出了可检验的物理解释。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a seismology-guided multi-agent AI system that autonomously plans and executes seismic analysis workflows while preserving auditable evidence chains, successfully recovering delayed cascading activation in the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and proposing a testable interpretation of progressive megathrust destabilization in the 2025-2026 Sanriku sequence.
